verified_diagnosis: The original test built App and ResearchHub directly but omitted cli.session worker_ui.bind and ui_persistence.bind. Its 50 v keys therefore executed 50 synchronous Store.save_ui/ui_state.write calls on the UI thread; cProfile verifies that chain.

Production cli.session gives ResearchHub and UIWriter the same WorkerScheduler. The fixture now uses one shared scheduler with independent source and research lanes, binds worker_ui/UIWriter, and passes it into ResearchHub; it introduces no additional executor.

The blocked-read loop still executes all 50 down/v/tick/compose iterations and retains the future identity, pending-read, cold-selection, navigation, exact copied bytes, remote-worker ownership and three-call assertions.

Pending result/exception/condition waits, UI-thread sleep, synchronous preference I/O and direct remote operations are rejected independently of elapsed time. Blocking attempts are recorded so a swallowed exception cannot evade the assertion.

The 0.5-second UI-thread CPU bound limits actual frame work; wall time is measured and included in failure diagnostics. CPU alone would hide waiting, which is why deterministic no-blocking guards are required too.

Clipboard copying was already asynchronous. The test now waits at most five seconds for each accepted copy only after the remote read is released and the guarded section has ended, then polls completion and retains the exact byte assertion. Five seconds matches the existing finish(hub) explicit test barrier.

implementation: Inject the fake through a module-local subprocess proxy only for this exact command on the test owner thread; preserve process-wide PATH, environment and subprocess.Popen.
